label: tp-prod-30y
_why: STAGE 2 OF THE TREATY-PORT PROBES (user, 2026-10-18: "If OK, implement likely production values and go with three 30-year probes to check performance. If OK, continue each of the 3 probes to 100-year completion."). The production book: the next-arm book (canon + WORLD_MARKET_MONOPOLY_THRESHOLD 0.99) + the treaty-port desire (production table) + the yearly driver against recognised hosts (calibrated over four 10-year probes, 20261019_002008 / _004649 / _011240 / _013756; the chosen variant tpd4: the desire x4 - ranking unchanged - and the driver at 10% a year, desire >= 60, 8-year cooldown, free host, no great-power hosts: 0-11% of active war goals, new ports in recognised hosts (Two Sicilies -> France, Ottomans -> Britain)). The question is PERFORMANCE: does the desire block (evaluated by the engine for every potential treaty-port state) and the driver (a yearly ordered_state over coastal states for ~15-25 AIs) cost tick time?

_arms.tpd4: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.jex-dam4s-rs-x25-m10ac-dpriv-wm99-tpd4.json} - the chosen production book; + telemetry. Also carries the isolationism fix (0b7b2ad).

_comparison: Wall clock per in-game year 1836-1866 against the three canon-family runs of 20261016_092158_rs-m10ac-n3 (the same machine two days earlier; that book lacks private dams, the monopoly define and the isolationism fix) and the vanilla n=16 baseline (the 10% budget, CLAUDE.md). Read with tools/testbed/ledger/wall_clusters.mjs and slow_episodes.mjs (the ruled clusters), and the war-goal mix from the v19 summaries.

_predictions.performance: seconds per in-game year within the seed spread of the reference (a few %): the desire is one small script value per potential state per AI update and the driver a yearly ordered_state for at most ~25 countries
_predictions.wars: treaty-port demands stay under the 10% guard set in stage 1c; more wars than the reference only by the driven plays

_stop_rule: none: three fixed runs, then each continued to 1936 (user-ordered).
